signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Divergence
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +43.5k faces severe liquidations as AUD underperforms across the board, dropping to 0.5627 on Friday against a surging Swiss Franc. Safe-haven inflows and a top-ranked Swiss Economic Surprise Index (+35.9) contrast with AUD's post-hike selloff, overriding the nominal carry advantage. The upcoming Asian open tests whether 0.5600 psychological support holds under bilateral momentum. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF into the Sydney open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open liquidity resumption. Risk: A rebound above 0.5700 driven by broad risk stabilization.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded COT Short Squeeze Risk
signals.text: EUR COT LF short sits at an extreme -104.0k contracts (52-week percentile of 2, z = -1.80) while Friday closed at 1.1143 following robust US nonfarm payrolls (+165k). Strong US employment solidifies the Fed's restrictive real rate (+1.61%) and reinforces SOFR carry over €STR (+148bp), yet one-sided institutional shorts leave downside extensions vulnerable to abrupt profit-taking. The upcoming US CPI release and the 9 Dec Fed meeting will dictate whether euro bears can breach the 1.1100 handle. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD with caution on crowded positioning. Catalyst: next Fed meeting (mkt: 89% hike priced) on 9 Dec. Risk: A daily close above the 20-day SMA at 1.1195 triggering short covering.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Labor Divergence & COT Imbalance
signals.text: CAD COT LF net short stands at -85.3k contracts as USD/CAD surged to 1.4128 on Friday, breaking above its 10-day high following diverging employment prints. A blowout US nonfarm payrolls beat (+165k) contrasted sharply with Canadian job contraction (-4.7k), widening the 2Y yield gap against Canada to -142bp alongside a +140bp OIS carry advantage for USD. Momentum targets a retest of 1.4200 into the week ahead. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD above 1.4070. Catalyst: next BoC meeting (mkt: 44% hike priced) on 9 Dec. Risk: A retracement below the 20-day SMA at 1.4069 invalidating the breakout.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew vs Yield Gap
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 158.43, confronting extreme 1M risk reversals of -1.97 that reflect heightened institutional demand for downside puts despite a +269bp OIS carry advantage favoring the dollar. Widening US-Japan rate differentials and a bear-steepening US curve maintain underlying spot support, but heavy downside options pricing warns of rapid unwinds if geopolitical tension spikes. The 18 Dec BoJ meeting determines whether domestic policy normalization can dismantle the carry trade. Trade bias: Neutral-to-bullish USD/JPY above 157.96. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 72% hike priced) on 18 Dec. Risk: A break below the 50-day SMA at 157.30 triggering put-option cascades.
